newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS-China EB in US$1.05 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS-China EB in US$1.05 bln loan.

text.p: China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd nipped in late Friday evening with its long-awaited loan to partly fund its purchase of 7.74 percent of Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd.

Everbright Finance and Investment Co Ltd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of China Everbright Holdings Co, has awarded a mandate for a US$1.05 billion 12-month loan to finance up to 70 percent of its purchase of the Hongkong Telecom stake.
The all-in would be 45 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate, and drawdown is on or before June 6, China Everbright Holdings Co said.
Deadline for the Hongkong Telecom purchase stake is June 3.
It said the Hongkong Telecom shares would be security for the loan, which will carry a guarantee from China Everbright Holdings Co.
China Everbright agreed on May 9 to buy 7.74 percent of Hongkong Telecom from CITIC Pacific Ltd at a purchase price of HK$12.60 a share, or a total of HK$11.4 billion.
China Everbright Holdings Co is a holding company controlled by China's State Council.
China Everbright Holding Co also announced a five-year US$150 million five-year floating-rate note (FRN) being arranged by a group of Singapore banks, bankers said.
The FRN includes a put option in year three and was priced at par to float at 60 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate, bankers said.

Fees are 25 basis points for co-lead managers committing US$10 million, 20 basis points for senior managers committing US$7 million to US$9 million, and 15 basis points committing US$5 million to US$6 million.
The issue is being arranged by Development Bank of Singapore, Oversea Chinese Banking Corp, United Overseas Bank, Overseas Union Bank, and Keppel Bank.
International Finance Corp of Thailand (IFCT) was expected to launch its US$150 million FRN this week, but has held it over until next week.

Bank of East Asia (BEA) signed the HK$2.6 billion FRCD issue due June 3, 2000 with 21 international financial institutions, its second under a HK$18 billion CD programme, and its third Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) eligible issue.
The FRCD would help BEA meet strong demand for syndicated loans, structured finance and consumer finance, chairman and chief executive David Li said at the signing ceremony.
The three-year certificates were issued at par to float at 30 basis points over the three-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return for top-tier managers is 37 basis points.
